journeys.name: Prefix worked out for you
journeys.idea: The person gives the exported settings and where they go; the system validates, works out the key prefix and reports what it found before applying.
journeys.tradeoff: Relies on the guess being right for the first key, so the person must still read the prefix the system proposes.

steps.intent: Choose the exported machine settings and the policy source (user or computer) they should be brought into.
steps.system: The system accepts only exported-settings files and remembers the chosen source.

link.reason: File and destination are given together instead of in separate steps.

steps.intent: Be told what the file contains and how its keys will be named in the source.
steps.system: The system checks the file is a genuine export, ignores blank and comment lines, reads keys, removals, deletions and default values, works out the key prefix from the first key, and warns when the file holds default values or the prefix could not be worked out.

link.reason: The system derives the prefix and the warnings instead of making the person type or discover them.

steps.intent: Give a prefix only if the system could not decide one.
steps.system: The system refuses to continue without a file or a prefix and says which is missing.

link.reason: The prefix is asked only in the rare case it is unknown.

steps.intent: Bring the settings into the source.
steps.system: The system removes marked keys, deletes marked values, saves the others with the prefix removed from names, tells the person only that the import failed if it does, then refreshes what the person sees.

link.reason: Applying and refreshing are one outcome rather than separate actions.

steps.intent: Leave without importing.
steps.system: The system changes nothing.

link.reason: Backing out stays available at every point.

journeys.recommended: Fewest decisions: the prefix, which people rarely know, is asked only when the system cannot work it out, and what was found is reported before anything is applied.

journeys.name: Guided import
journeys.idea: A short prompted path: pick the file, review what was found, confirm the prefix, then apply.
journeys.tradeoff: More steps than the automated path, but each is explained for people who import rarely.

steps.intent: Say which exported settings file to bring in.
steps.system: The system accepts only exported-settings files and refuses when none is given.

link.reason: Starting with the file makes the purpose of the task clear.

steps.intent: Read what the system found in the file.
steps.system: The system validates the file, ignores blank and comment lines, interprets keys, removals, deletions, default values and value forms, and warns about default values.

link.reason: Reading and reviewing become a visible step rather than a hidden side effect of choosing.

steps.intent: Confirm the proposed key prefix.
steps.system: The system proposes a prefix worked out from the first key and, if it could not, says so and leaves it for the person to fill; a prefix is required.

link.reason: A proposed prefix replaces a blank entry.

steps.intent: Choose the policy source that receives the settings and apply.
steps.system: The system applies the file to the chosen source, refreshes what is shown, and reports a failure plainly.

link.reason: The destination is chosen last, with the result in view.

steps.intent: Cancel at any time.
steps.system: The system changes nothing.

link.reason: Backing out stays available.

journeys.name: One request
journeys.idea: The person names the policy file and the source it belongs to; the system loads it and says whether it worked.
journeys.tradeoff: Loads at once, so a wrong choice is only corrected by not saving.

steps.intent: Bring a policy file into the user or computer policy source.
steps.system: The system reads the file and applies it as the difference from an empty file so nothing is forgotten, or says the file could not be loaded and changes nothing.

link.reason: The task is already one request and stays so.

steps.intent: Know that the result is held until saved.
steps.system: The system says the import succeeded and keeps the change in memory until the person saves.

link.reason: Making the held state explicit avoids surprise about what is stored.

journeys.recommended: Smallest shape that meets the outcome: one request, one clear result, and nothing is written until the person saves.

journeys.name: Preview then apply
journeys.idea: The system reads the file first, then the person decides to apply it to the chosen source.
journeys.tradeoff: Adds a confirming step to a task that is already short.

steps.intent: Choose the policy file and the source it should go into.
steps.system: The system reads the file and tells the person if it cannot be loaded, changing nothing.

link.reason: Reading before applying lets problems surface before anything changes.

steps.intent: Apply it.
steps.system: The system applies the file as the difference from an empty file, says the import was successful and keeps it in memory until saved.

link.reason: Applying is a deliberate second decision.

journeys.name: Export what is selected
journeys.idea: The person only names the file; the system proposes the branch and prefix from what is being edited and exports.
journeys.tradeoff: Defaults can be wrong for unusual cases, so they must be visible and changeable.

steps.intent: Say where to write the exported settings.
steps.system: The system refuses to continue until a file name is given, and proposes the selected branch (or the whole policy file if none) and a prefix that fits the source being edited, user or machine.

link.reason: Branch and prefix are filled in so only the file is required.

steps.intent: Adjust the branch or prefix only if the default is not what is wanted.
steps.system: The system uses the text given as is, with any trailing separator on a branch removed.

link.reason: The rare adjustment no longer stands in front of every export.

steps.intent: Receive the settings file, or back out.
steps.system: The system takes the source as is when it is a policy file, or rebuilds it from the three policy locations with each value keeping its type when it comes from the machine settings, writes it with removals and deletions marked and values in the exported-settings format, and tells the person it worked or only that it failed, letting the person retry. Backing out writes nothing.

link.reason: Building and writing are one outcome for the person.

drops.reason: An unsupported source raising an unhandled error is a defect that no known source reaches; the target reports any problem to the person plainly instead.

journeys.recommended: Most exports need only a file name; branch and prefix are proposed from what is being edited and can be changed when needed.

journeys.name: Choose, then name
journeys.idea: Built around the outcome: decide what to export, decide how its keys are named, then name the file.
journeys.tradeoff: More decisions up front than the proposal-based path.

steps.intent: Decide how much of the policy source to export.
steps.system: The system starts with the selected branch, or all of it when nothing is selected; the person may change it, and a trailing separator is removed.

link.reason: The scope of the export is the first thing to know.

steps.intent: Decide how the exported keys should be named.
steps.system: The system proposes a user prefix when editing the user source and a machine prefix otherwise; the person may change it and it is used unchecked.

link.reason: A proposed prefix replaces a blank entry.

steps.intent: Name the file to write.
steps.system: The system refuses to continue until a file name is given.

link.reason: The destination is the last decision.

steps.intent: Receive the settings file, or back out at any time.
steps.system: The system builds the source (rebuilt from the machine settings when needed), writes it in the exported-settings format, and tells the person it worked or only that it failed. Backing out writes nothing.

link.reason: Writing is one outcome, and backing out is always possible.

drops.reason: An unsupported source raising an unhandled error is a defect that no known source reaches; the target reports any problem to the person plainly instead.

journeys.name: One request
journeys.idea: The person names the area and the file; the system writes the policy file and says whether it worked.
journeys.tradeoff: No preview of what is written.

steps.intent: Save a policy source out as a policy file.
steps.system: The system writes the chosen area's source, whatever holds it, as a policy file and tells the person it worked or that it could not be saved.

link.reason: Already one request; adding steps would not help.

journeys.recommended: The task is a single outcome; one request and one clear result.

journeys.name: Current area proposed
journeys.idea: The system proposes the area being edited, so the person only confirms where to save.
journeys.tradeoff: Wrong when the person wants the other area, so the choice must stay visible.

steps.intent: Say where to save the policy file for the area being edited.
steps.system: The system proposes the area currently being edited, and the person may choose the other one.

link.reason: Most people export what they are editing.

steps.intent: Receive the policy file.
steps.system: The system writes the area's source as a policy file and says it was exported successfully or could not be saved.

link.reason: Choosing and writing are separate so the result is clearly reported.

journeys.name: Pick a source, then load
journeys.idea: The person picks where definitions come from, says whether to replace or add, and the system loads and remembers.
journeys.tradeoff: Still a few decisions, but each is shown only when it applies.

steps.intent: Choose where the definitions come from: the system's standard folder, the domain's shared folder, or a folder of the person's own.
steps.system: The system offers the domain choice only when the computer is joined to a domain and that folder exists, starts on the person's own folder, and makes the folder entry usable only for that choice.

link.reason: The available sources are discovered by the system, not tried by the person.

steps.intent: Decide whether to replace what is loaded or add to it.
steps.system: The system proposes replacing, and passes the choice on only when an existing folder was accepted.

link.reason: Replacing is the usual intent, so it is proposed.

steps.intent: Load the definitions.
steps.system: The system uses the standard, domain or typed folder, refuses one that does not exist, empties the workspace first only when replacing, reports problems without stopping, and on failure says the folder could not be fully added with the reason.

link.reason: Checking and loading are one outcome.

steps.intent: Have the folder remembered for next time.
steps.system: The system remembers the folder only when the workspace was replaced and the load did not fail.

link.reason: Remembering is a visible consequence of replacing.

steps.intent: Cancel at any time.
steps.system: No folder is chosen.

link.reason: Backing out stays available.

journeys.name: Load without questions
journeys.idea: The person gives one folder; the system decides replace or add from what is already loaded.
journeys.tradeoff: Less control by default over replace versus add.

steps.intent: Choose the folder of definitions to load.
steps.system: The system lists the standard folder and, only when it exists on a joined domain, the domain folder, alongside the person's own; it checks the folder exists and refuses one that does not.

link.reason: Discovering, picking and checking happen together.

steps.intent: Say whether to replace what is already loaded, only when something is loaded.
steps.system: The system proposes replacing, and does not ask when nothing is loaded.

link.reason: The question appears only when it matters.

steps.intent: Get the definitions loaded.
steps.system: The system empties the workspace first only when replacing, adds the folder, reports problems without stopping, and on failure says the folder could not be fully added with the reason; it remembers the folder only when replacing succeeded.

link.reason: The system works out what to do rather than asking for each aspect.

steps.intent: Cancel at any time.
steps.system: No folder is chosen.

link.reason: Backing out stays available.

journeys.recommended: Fewest decisions: one folder, and replace-or-add is asked only when something is already loaded.

journeys.name: Add one file
journeys.idea: The person chooses one template file; the system adds it alone to what is loaded.
journeys.tradeoff: Adding several files means repeating the task.

steps.intent: Choose one policy template file to add.
steps.system: The system accepts only template files.

link.reason: One file, one request.

steps.intent: See it added.
steps.system: The system adds that file alone without emptying the workspace, does not remember it as the definitions folder, builds the structures, and reports one failure with the reason if refused.

link.reason: The result is a clear second beat.

journeys.name: Add several at once
journeys.idea: The person chooses one or more template files and the system adds each in turn and reports each failure.
journeys.tradeoff: Each added file may fail separately, so the result is a list rather than one message.

steps.intent: Choose the policy template files to add.
steps.system: The system accepts only template files, one or several.

link.reason: One request covers any number of files.

steps.intent: See what was added and what was refused.
steps.system: The system adds each file alone without emptying the workspace or remembering a folder, builds the structures once, and reports each refused file with its reason.

link.reason: The system handles the repetition.

journeys.recommended: Real work often adds a handful of files; one request avoids repeating the task for each.

journeys.name: Clear at once
journeys.idea: One request empties the workspace immediately.
journeys.tradeoff: No safety net if requested by mistake.

steps.intent: Remove all loaded definitions.
steps.system: The system empties the workspace at once with no confirmation and rebuilds what is shown.

link.reason: Already a single outcome.

journeys.name: Clear with a way back
journeys.idea: Clearing stays immediate, and the system says what was removed and offers to put it back.
journeys.tradeoff: The system must keep what was removed until the person moves on.

steps.intent: Remove all loaded definitions.
steps.system: The system empties the workspace at once with no confirmation and rebuilds what is shown.

link.reason: Immediate, as people expect.

steps.intent: Undo it if it was a mistake.
steps.system: The system says what was removed and restores it on request.

link.reason: A mistaken clear currently means reloading everything from the folders.

journeys.recommended: No confirmation is added, yet a mistaken clear is no longer costly.

journeys.name: List then details
journeys.idea: See the loaded template files, then choose one to see what it contributes.
journeys.tradeoff: Two steps for the simplest question.

steps.intent: See which template files are loaded.
steps.system: The system lists the loaded template files with their namespaces.

link.reason: The list answers the first half of the outcome.

steps.intent: Choose a file to see what it contributes.
steps.system: The system shows only the policies, categories with sub-categories, products with versions and support rules defined in that file, and only for a chosen file.

link.reason: Every way of opening details is one choice.

drops.reason: Keeping a column filling the width is a property of one kind of interface, not of the task.
Opening details without a chosen file is an inconsistency; the target opens details only for a chosen file.

journeys.name: Contribution at a glance
journeys.idea: The list itself shows what each file contributes; details are one step further when wanted.
journeys.tradeoff: Counts must be kept in step with what the file defines.

steps.intent: See which files are loaded and roughly what each contributes.
steps.system: The system lists the loaded files with the number of policies, categories, products and support rules each defines.

link.reason: The system summarises instead of making the person open each file.

steps.intent: Look closer at one file.
steps.system: The system shows exactly what was defined in that file, for a chosen file only.

link.reason: Detail is on demand.

drops.reason: Keeping a column filling the width is a property of one kind of interface, not of the task.
Opening details without a chosen file is an inconsistency; the target opens details only for a chosen file.

journeys.recommended: Most questions are answered by the list alone, so details are optional.
